## Learning outcomes {.unnumbered #sec-m1-outcomes}

By the end of this session you should be able to:

1. Derive, from arithmetic against a measured noise floor and quantization
   step, why a strain-gauge bridge needs an instrumentation amplifier and how
   much gain it needs.
2. Separate the four things a static mechanical calibration has to tell
   apart — linearity, hysteresis, creep, zero drift — and measure each one
   with the right procedure.
3. Explain, with the bridge equation, why quarter, half and full bridge
   wiring differ in sensitivity and in what they cancel, and choose between
   them for a stated goal.
4. Design and run a temperature-compensation test, and quantify — not just
   assert — what a dummy gauge buys.
5. Build a GUM uncertainty budget for a measured strain, with correct
   sensitivity coefficients for a chain of gauge, amplifier and converter.

## Prerequisites {#sec-m1-prerequisites}

- [S1](../S1-daq-static/index.qmd), completed: this experiment uses its
  noise floor and effective-quantization results directly, without
  re-deriving them.
- [The beam rig](../../hardware/beam-rig.qmd) and [the conditioning
  board](../../hardware/conditioning-board.qmd), read once: this handbook
  uses their symbols and equations without repeating the derivations.
- Statistics: mean, standard deviation, least squares. No more.

## Data recording {#sec-m1-recording}

Twenty-four runs, twenty-four CSV files, twenty-four sidecars. The format is
specified in [Data format](../../data-format/index.qmd); the checklist in
@sec-m1-step-sidecar is the version to work through at the bench. M1 extends
the channel schema with a few extra keys, the same way [S3
does](../S3-aliasing-filtering/handbook.qmd#sec-s3-recording):

```{.yaml filename="data/bridge-quarter-010.yaml"}
experiment: M1
run: bridge-quarter-010
date: 2026-09-18
operator: "your name"
synthetic: false

board:
  model: portenta-h7
  serial: "from arduino-io list"
  usbio_version: "from arduino-io info"
  adc_bits: 16
  vref_mV: 3300

host:
  os: linux
  os_version: "from uname -a"
  machine: "which bench"
  hub: true

driver_version: "0.4.0"
binding: cli

acquisition:
  pins: [15]
  requested_period_us: 1000
  achieved_rate_hz: 0.0      # from the stream summary
  duration_s: 0.2

stream_stats:                 # all six, from the summary line
  records: 0
  device_overruns: 0
  seq_gaps: 0
  host_drops: 0
  resyncs: 0
  stale_records: 0

channels:
  - pin: 15
    quantity: force
    unit: N
    sensor: "strain gauge, quarter bridge"
    conditioning:
      gain: 11314.3            # measured, from the DC verification of @sec-m1-step-identify
      offset: 0.165
      filter: none
    calibration_reference: "reference mass at the beam tip"
    reference_value: 0.0980665  # F = m g, from the applied mass
    reference_u: 0.00049        # from the mass/balance uncertainty
    bridge_type: quarter        # M1 extension: quarter, half or full
    gauge_factor: 2.1           # M1 extension: from the gauge's datasheet
    u_gauge_factor_rel: 0.005   # M1 extension
    bridge_excitation_v: 5.0    # M1 extension
    u_excitation_rel: 0.005     # M1 extension
    amplifier_u_gain_rel: 0.01  # M1 extension
    amplifier_u_offset_v: 0.01  # M1 extension

environment:
  ambient_temperature_C: 23.0
  notes: ""

references:
  - instrument: "reference masses"
    model: "the model you used"
    calibration: "certificate or none"
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Record the mass in newtons, not kilograms

`reference_value` is in the channel's declared `unit`, which for every
mechanical run here is `N`. Convert with $F = mg$ before writing it down —
writing the mass in kilograms into a field documented as newtons breaks
every downstream calculation silently.
:::

## Analysis tasks {#sec-m1-tasks}

Open one of the two templates —
[Python](analysis-py.qmd) or [R](analysis-r.qmd) — point it at your files,
and work through it. They contain the same sections and produce the same
numbers.

1. **Data quality.** Run `validate_meta()` on every sidecar, as in S1.
2. **In-amp arithmetic.** Reproduce @eq-m1-quarter-numeric and
   @eq-m1-required-gain with the sidecar's own gauge factor, excitation and
   amplifier gain, and confirm the amplifier actually built matches what the
   arithmetic demands.
3. **Load cell.** Fit @eq-m1-linearity to the loading sweep; compute
   @eq-m1-hysteresis from the loading/unloading pair; fit @eq-m1-creep to
   the held-load run; compare the first and last zero for zero drift.
4. **Bridge configurations.** Compute the sensitivity of quarter, half and
   full bridge from the beam-tip sweep and check the 1 : 2 : 4 ratio of
   @eq-m1-bridge-configs.
5. **Temperature compensation.** Apply @eq-m1-temp-apparent to both
   configurations and report the apparent strain per kelvin for each.
6. **Budget.** Build the budget of @sec-m1-budget below.

## Uncertainty budget {#sec-m1-budget}

{{< include ../../shared/_uncertainty-budget.qmd >}}

M1's budget is built for the **beam-mounted quarter bridge's strain**,
$\hat\varepsilon$ from @eq-m1-strain-recover, at the reference point of the
quarter-bridge sweep — see @sec-m1-budget-choice for why this measurand
rather than the load cell's force.

| Component | Type | Distribution | Source | $c_i$ |
|---|:--:|---|---|---|
| Repeatability of $\Delta V$ | A | — | $\sigma/\sqrt{n}$ from the sweep point's own repeats | $4/(kV_\mathrm{ex})$ |
| Effective quantization | B | Rectangular | Half-width $q_\mathrm{eff}/2$ from [S1's ENOB method](../S1-daq-static/handbook.qmd#eq-s1-enob), applied locally | $4/(kV_\mathrm{ex})$ |
| Amplifier gain $G$ | B | Rectangular | `amplifier_u_gain_rel` in the sidecar | $-\hat\varepsilon/G$ |
| Amplifier offset | B | Rectangular | `amplifier_u_offset_v` | $-4/(kV_\mathrm{ex}G)$ |
| Gauge factor $k$ | B | Rectangular | `u_gauge_factor_rel` | $-\hat\varepsilon/k$ |
| Excitation voltage $V_\mathrm{ex}$ | B | Rectangular | `u_excitation_rel` | $-\hat\varepsilon/V_\mathrm{ex}$ |

: Components of the M1 budget {#tbl-m1-components}

Report $u_c$ and $U = 2u_c$, the index $h_i$ of every component, and one
sentence naming the dominant term and what you would change to reduce it.

::: {.callout-important}
## What this budget leaves out, and why

The load cell's own hysteresis and creep are real uncertainty sources for a
*force* measurement, but this budget's measurand is strain from the
beam-mounted quarter bridge, a physically different sensor with negligible
mechanical hysteresis of its own (a bonded foil gauge, unlike a load cell's
internal spring element). Building the load cell's own force budget instead
— with hysteresis and creep as Type B bounds, following [the conditioning
board's treatment](../../hardware/conditioning-board.qmd#sec-cond-budget) —
is a direct and instructive extension.
:::

## Questions {#sec-m1-questions}

1. @eq-m1-quarter-numeric used $\varepsilon = 10^{-4}$. Recompute it for
   $\varepsilon = 10^{-5}$ (ten times smaller, still a realistic strain) and
   say whether the amplifier sized by @eq-m1-required-gain for the original
   strain would clip, under-use the range, or still be about right.
2. Your loading and unloading curves cross at $F = 0$ and at
   $F = F_\mathrm{cap}$ by construction (@eq-m1-hysteresis). Explain, from
   the bridge physics, why a real load cell's hysteresis loop should also
   close at both ends, and what it would mean physically if it did not.
3. The half-bridge temperature test does not read exactly zero. Using your
   own $\alpha_\mathrm{apparent}$ figures, express the half bridge's
   compensation as a percentage reduction relative to the bare quarter
   bridge, and say what would improve it further.
4. A colleague wires a half bridge with both gauges on the beam (top and
   bottom surfaces at the same $x$) instead of one active gauge and one
   dummy. Does this configuration cancel temperature, axial load, both or
   neither? Justify from @eq-m1-bridge-configs and @sec-m1-bridges.
5. Your creep fit gives $\tau$ and $C_\infty$ from @eq-m1-creep. If the hold
   had been half as long, would you expect $\tau$ to change? Would you
   expect your estimate of $C_\infty$ to be as reliable? Explain the
   difference.
6. In @tbl-m1-components, which component's sensitivity coefficient would
   change if you had budgeted the load cell's force instead of the
   beam-mounted gauge's strain? Which would stay essentially the same?
7. Using your fitted quarter-bridge sensitivity $d\varepsilon/dF$ and the
   placeholder beam dimensions your reference data was generated with, what
   additional information would you need to recover Young's modulus $E$
   alone? (See [the beam rig's stiffness
   cross-check](../../hardware/beam-rig.qmd#sec-beam-relations) and
   [M2](../M2-hall-displacement/index.qmd).)
